answer.answer: The coach itinerary is only a sample; passenger-specific airline confirmations establish the booked trip. The youth travels ahead to Brussels and later transfers to Geneva, the rest of the family meets the youth there, and all four return together from Milan Linate. Because the return is from Linate—not Malpensa—the northern Italy finish remains feasible, but the plan should preserve a final night in Milan and remain compatible with Linate departure logistics.

claims.value: The ski-team packet contains a coach sample itinerary with example booking references, not proof of passenger bookings. Passenger-specific airline confirmations reviewed on 2026-07-22 are authoritative for booked flights and supersede the packet’s sample flights; confirmation codes are omitted from the public fixture.

The youth traveler’s confirmed outbound is Seattle to Amsterdam to Brussels on August 4-5, 2026, followed by Brussels to Geneva on August 10, 2026. An official schedule-change notice checked on 2026-07-26 06:20 PDT moved the August 10 departure 85 minutes earlier; its flight number and airports are unchanged, but the camp-transfer timing must be adjusted.

The family’s confirmed outbound is Seattle to London Heathrow to Geneva on August 9-10, 2026. The shared return has all four travelers—including the youth traveler—flying Milan Linate to London Heathrow to Seattle on August 25, 2026.

The confirmed return departs Milan Linate, not Milan Malpensa. This keeps the northern Italy finish feasible, but planning must keep that finish compatible with Linate and should place the final night in Milan before the August 25, 2026 departure.

answer.answer: Straylight is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth. The current-status note controls; the older green checkpoint is historical and explicitly superseded by production-sized timeout and full-manifest-copy findings. The approved direction is a Markdown-first architecture with changed-file versioning, rebuildable derived data, precise checkpoint references, coherent hydration, and compact retrieval packets.

claims.value: Projects/Straylight current status.md, updated 2026-07-26T12:00:00-07:00, is the controlling implementation truth. Projects/Straylight stale checkpoint.md, recorded 2026-07-23T18:00:00-07:00, is historical: its passing test corpus, healthy `/ready` configuration, and immediate-owner-alpha proposal predate the production-sized findings and must not override the newer note. Current status says the architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth.

Broad `memory.open` and lexical retrieval are slow and can hit the 30-second database timeout. Because retrieval lanes share one transaction, failure in a later lane can also discard an earlier successful lane. Connection, authentication, and exact-path reads work, but these production retrieval failures prevent dependable owner readiness.

Normal writes copy a full corpus membership manifest. With about 64,000 active records and 9.6 million estimated source tokens already present, this creates write amplification that makes the current architecture unsuitable for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth.

The approved simplification is to make current Markdown files the workspace truth; version only changed files; make indexes and derived views rebuildable; checkpoint using exact path, version, and hash references plus changes since a workspace generation; and retain coherent source hydration and compact retrieval packets. This is the approved direction, not a verified completed implementation.
